resources.string: Scan the code on your computer
Open Fenpo on Windows and show the code on the screen to the camera. Both must be on the same Wi‑Fi network.
Fenpo needs the camera to read the code.
Camera access is off. Turn it on in Fenpo’s settings.
This is not a Fenpo code. Scan the code in the Fenpo window on Windows.
The code could not be read completely. Show it again in Fenpo on Windows and hold the phone still.
This code comes from a newer Fenpo. Update Fenpo on this phone.
Choose your computer in the window that opens. If it is not listed, keep Fenpo open on Windows and turn on Location on the phone; Android needs it to search.
Keep the phone near the computer and accept the pairing request on both. If it keeps failing, remove the computer in Bluetooth settings and try again.
This code belongs to another computer
Can’t set up an encrypted connection
The code is no longer valid
The phone and the computer must be on the same Wi‑Fi network. Check that Fenpo is open on Windows and that the firewall lets it through.
The security check failed. Scan the current code in Fenpo on Windows again. If it happens again, a device on the network may be in between.
Make sure both apps are up to date, then scan the code again.
Each code works once and for a few minutes. Scan the new code on Windows.
Choose Allow in the window on Windows, then try again.
Update Fenpo on the phone and on the computer.
The approval window on Windows may still be open. Scan the code again.
Scan the code again. If it happens again, update both apps.
Finds your computer over Bluetooth and Wi‑Fi
Transfers and clipboard from your PC
Your phone’s notifications show up on your PC
Without it the connection stays up all day
Messages are read and sent from your PC
If you see “Restricted setting”: Settings > Apps > Fenpo > ⋮ > Allow restricted settings, then come back here. Android asks for this when an app is installed outside a store.
